title: Signal comparison: advanced bar chart techniques

blocks.content: Start a standalone lab that turns synthetic signals into a saved comparison chart.

blocks.tooltip: Begin from the specified workspace for this part of the lab.
blocks.content: Open Dashboards to begin with a saved workspace.
You have opened the workspace where this independent dashboard will begin.
Prepare a synthetic data source if one is missing; existing TestData automatically completes this setup on Cloud or OSS.
Create and test **TestData** if needed.

steps.tooltip: Begin from the specified workspace for this part of the lab.
steps.description: Open the shared Add data source page.

steps.tooltip: Find the built-in synthetic option without connecting an external service.
steps.description: Find TestData; no external service or credentials are needed. Set the value to `TestData`.

steps.tooltip: Create a reusable source of generated practice samples.
Confirm that the generated samples are available.
steps.description: Check that the synthetic source works.

blocks.content: You can reuse an existing synthetic source, while creating one requires administrator access and no external credentials.

whenTrue.prompt: Select your TestData source; its name may differ in your organization.

blocks.content: Create a fresh panel and select the source that will supply your practice signals.

blocks.tooltip: Begin from the specified workspace for this part of the lab.
blocks.content: Create a fresh dashboard for this lab.

blocks.tooltip: Add space for the synthetic comparison.
blocks.content: Add a panel for your synthetic signals.

blocks.tooltip: Open the controls for data and presentation.
blocks.content: Open the visualization editor.

blocks.tooltip: Use the source name selected earlier in this guide.
blocks.content: Use the TestData source you selected. Set the value to `{{practiceSource}}`.
Choose **Bar chart**.

steps.tooltip: Choose a display suited to categorical comparisons.
Compare numeric summaries across named categories.

blocks.tooltip: Make the result recognizable when you return to it.
blocks.content: Give the panel a recognizable name. Set the value to `Signal comparison`.
You have a named comparison panel connected to your chosen synthetic source.
Generate three random walks bounded from 0 to 100, each starting at 50.

blocks.tooltip: Prevent generated samples from falling below zero.
blocks.content: Keep the synthetic values at or above zero. Set the value to `0`.

blocks.tooltip: Keep generated samples within the practice range.
blocks.content: Cap the synthetic values at 100. Set the value to `100`.

blocks.tooltip: Begin each generated walk halfway through the range.
blocks.content: Start the random walk halfway through the range. Set the value to `50`.

blocks.tooltip: Create enough signals for a categorical comparison.
blocks.content: Generate 3 synthetic signals. Set the value to `3`.

blocks.tooltip: Generate samples using the settings you just entered.
blocks.content: Run the query to see your practice data.
You have produced bounded practice signals for learning visual interpretation without implying real service health.

blocks.question: What do the three bounded random walks represent?

choices.text: Synthetic practice signals for learning chart interpretation.
choices.hint: The samples are generated for this lab and have no production meaning.

choices.text: Measurements proving the health of three production services.
choices.hint: The samples are generated for this lab and have no production meaning.

blocks.content: Reduce the samples to one category per signal and compare its peak with its average.
Add **Reduce** to summarize the signals.

steps.tooltip: Reshape the samples before displaying them.
Summarize many samples into comparable statistics.
steps.description: Add Reduce to summarize each signal.

blocks.tooltip: Produce a separate category for each signal.
blocks.content: Use one output row for each series. Set the value to `Series to rows`.

blocks.tooltip: Keep the existing peak statistic and include an average.
blocks.content: Add Mean alongside the default Max calculation. Set the value to `Mean`.

blocks.tooltip: Compare the peak and average within each signal category.
blocks.content: Compare three signal categories, each with a peak and average bar.
You have turned three time series into categorical rows with **Max** and **Mean** values.

blocks.question: Why keep peak and average as paired bars instead of stacking them?

choices.text: They are two summaries of the same samples, not parts of a meaningful total.
choices.hint: A peak and an average describe the same series in different ways; adding them is misleading.

choices.text: Their sum measures the total amount of signal traffic.
choices.hint: A peak and an average describe the same series in different ways; adding them is misleading.

blocks.content: Arrange the paired bars horizontally and tune spacing so each category is easy to compare.

blocks.tooltip: Give category labels room beside their values.
blocks.content: Use horizontal bars so category labels have room.

blocks.tooltip: Read the numbers without estimating lengths.
blocks.content: Print the values alongside the bars.

blocks.tooltip: Keep two summaries separate because their sum is not a meaningful total.
blocks.content: Keep the peak and mean side by side; they are not parts of a total.

blocks.tooltip: Separate categories while keeping each pair together.
blocks.content: Separate category groups while keeping paired bars close. Set the value to `0.7`.

blocks.tooltip: Leave space between neighboring comparisons.
blocks.content: Leave a small gap between neighboring bars. Set the value to `0.8`.

blocks.tooltip: Soften the corners slightly without changing their meaning.
blocks.content: Round the bar corners slightly. Set the value to `0.1`.

blocks.tooltip: Keep the displayed numbers concise.
blocks.content: Keep value labels concise with one decimal. Set the value to `1`.
You have kept peak and average side by side, with readable labels and distinct category groups.
Add subtle styling and shared context while keeping the synthetic scale honestly labeled.

blocks.tooltip: Add a thin boundary to distinguish neighboring fills.
blocks.content: Give each bar a thin outline. Set the value to `1`.

blocks.tooltip: Keep fills visible without making them fully opaque.
blocks.content: Keep the bars visible without making them opaque. Set the value to `80`.

blocks.tooltip: Fade the fill toward the baseline for a subtle treatment.
blocks.content: Fade the fill toward the baseline.

blocks.tooltip: Inspect both statistics together for a category.
blocks.content: Compare both statistics in one tooltip.

blocks.tooltip: Give the calculations distinct rows for reference.
blocks.content: Give the two calculations clear legend rows.

blocks.tooltip: Describe the synthetic scale without assigning a real unit.
blocks.content: Label the synthetic scale without implying a real unit. Set the value to `Illustrative value`.

blocks.tooltip: Compare the peak and average within each signal category.
blocks.content: Compare peak and mean within each category; a large gap suggests variability in the synthetic samples.
You can compare both statistics with a shared tooltip and table legend, without implying a real measurement unit.

blocks.question: What does a large gap between peak and average suggest here?

choices.hint: The chart summarizes synthetic samples, so the gap supports comparison rather than a service-health conclusion.

choices.text: Proof that a real service is failing.
choices.hint: The chart summarizes synthetic samples, so the gap supports comparison rather than a service-health conclusion.

blocks.content: Save the finished dashboard and inspect the retained comparison chart.

blocks.tooltip: Return with the configured panel ready to save.
blocks.content: Return to the dashboard.
Save the dashboard as Bar chart lab - Signal comparison.

steps.tooltip: Open the naming and persistence controls.
Give this lab a distinctive name for later retrieval.
steps.description: Name your saved dashboard. Set the value to `Bar chart lab - Signal comparison`.

blocks.tooltip: Confirm that the saved view retains the paired comparison and its labels.
blocks.content: Inspect the saved dashboard named Bar chart lab - Signal comparison: the Signal comparison panel should show three categories with horizontal, unstacked peak and average bars, visible values, distinct spacing, subtle gradient and outline, a table legend, and the axis label Illustrative value; inspect the shared tooltip to compare both statistics.
You have saved a standalone dashboard and checked the visible configuration you built.
